content: Itraconazole can increase the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is responsible for its metabolism. Both itraconazole and erythromycin lactobionate are known to prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. It is recommended to avoid this combination or consider alternative medications. Itraconazole similarly increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through CYP3A4 inhibition, with both drugs also prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. Esomeprazole can reduce the effectiveness of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH, which affects the solubility and absorption of itraconazole. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Avoid this combination or consider alternatives. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of eszopiclone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole elevates the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Everolimus is not recommended during itraconazole treatment and for two weeks after discontinuation of itraconazole. Famotidine reduces the effectiveness of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH, which impairs itraconazole absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid this combination or use alternatives. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, gradually increase the fedratinib dose to 300 mg/day for two weeks, then to 400 mg/day as tolerated. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, closely monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed until stable effects are achieved. Fentanyl is not recommended during itraconazole treatment and for two weeks after discontinuation of itraconazole. Itraconazole decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Fluconazole and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of intranasal fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, such as Cushing syndrome. Monitor for signs and symptoms of high corticosteroid concentrations. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Do not exceed an itraconazole dose of 200 mg/day in patients receiving fosamprenavir/ritonavir. Dose reductions may be needed for patients receiving fosamprenavir alone if itraconazole doses exceed 400 mg/day. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Co-administration of futibatinib with dual P-glycoprotein and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the incidence or severity of futibatinib toxicities. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Consider alternatives to strong CYP3A4 inhibitors when coadministered with gilteritinib. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Itraconazole and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid concomitant use of ibrutinib and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. Ibuprofen/famotidine reduces the effectiveness of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least two hours before or after itraconazole intake. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow recommendations for dosage modifications if adverse reactions occur. Idelalisib also increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Imipramine and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole and inhaled indacaterol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Isoflurane and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose (after at least five half-lives of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) to 500 mg daily. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Both drugs also decrease the QTc interval. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of ketamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lansoprazole reduces the effectiveness of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with lapatinib. If overlap in therapy cannot be avoided, consider reducing the lapatinib dose to 500 mg/day during and within one week of completing treatment with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration of larotrectinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior larotrectinib dose once the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued for 3–5 half-lives. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Levo-ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and itraconazole increases the levels or effects of levo-ketoconazole by the same mechanism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lofepramine and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole and lofexidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of lorlatinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase to the previous lorlatinib dose after three plasma half-lives of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor reduces the effectiveness of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for five half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the dose used before coadministration. Itraconazole and macimorelin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Maprotiline and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of itraconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam causes higher systemic exposure to midazolam, which may prolong sedation. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of nefazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce nilotinib to 300 mg daily in patients with resistant or intolerant Ph+ CML or to 200 mg daily in patients with newly diagnosed Ph+ CML-CP. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Itraconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Nizatidine reduces the effectiveness of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Nortriptyline and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism.
